claims.subject: Finite stochastic games with state-independent action sets
claims.scope: General finite stochastic-game existence; padding state-dependent actions is not silently semantics-preserving.

claims.subject: All finite quitting games
claims.scope: The quitting specialization is distinct from the general conjecture.

claims.subject: Two-player finite quitting games
claims.scope: All reward tables and all unilateral behavioral deviations.

claims.subject: Three-player finite quitting games (`Fin 3`)
claims.scope: All reward tables on the concrete player type `Fin 3`; reindexing is recorded separately.

claims.subject: Terminal approximate Nash existence and uniform-payoff existence
claims.scope: Finite quitting games; terminal approximate profiles are required at every positive error.

claims.subject: Quitting-game nonexistence and a fixed terminal exploitability gap
claims.scope: A counterexample must quantify over every behavioral profile.

claims.subject: Four-player quitting counterexample residual
claims.scope: For every supplied finite coordinate bound, a Fin 4 reward table has a uniform-equilibrium payoff or, on the same table, a terminal exploitability witness, full recursive normal core, all-player punishment normality, a normalized singleton packet with full support and an explicit positive coordinate floor, and ResidualHardClass. Thus the projective-Q-bar chamber is solved; the hard residual is not.

claims.subject: Finite principal dispatch in the four-player hard residual
claims.scope: Every supplied quantitative full-support hard residual has a size-two mutually harmful principal with outside positive helpers, or a size-three principal with an external positive helper or cyclic orientation and nonpositive determinant. This is singleton-matrix structure, not a semantic consumer.

claims.subject: Paid-chain refinement of the four-player strict-toggle residual
claims.scope: A bounded Fin 4 table with a terminal exploitability witness supplies, on the same table, full normal core, a quantitative full-support packet, and an actual reachable strict-toggle cycle. Its large-base branch is exactly a two-plus-two partition and enters the checked pure-or-mixed paid normal chain; the singleton-base and empty-base gaps remain.

claims.subject: Two-cycle lasso and hard-principal alignment
claims.scope: Every supplied Fin 4 hard residual has collision-anchored marked preemption geometry such that each of the eight two-cycle constructors uses its literal cycle pair as the nonprojective card-two crossing, or the geometry is one of the nine length-three/four cases. This formalizes alignment bookkeeping; it eliminates no semantic case and supplies no strategy consumer.

claims.subject: Terminal exploitability gaps for four-player full-core deadlock completions
claims.scope: For arbitrary nonsingleton coalition rewards, every terminal exploitability gap over a completion of the displayed normalized singleton matrix is at most 1227/96755; this does not prove that the gap vanishes or produce a uniform equilibrium.

claims.subject: Exact uniform equilibrium for the literal full-core deadlock completion
claims.scope: The named zero-multiquitter completion FullCoreDeadlock.reward has an exact uniform-equilibrium payoff, certified by a three-phase product block with supports {0}, {2}, and {1, 3}; arbitrary full-core completions retain only the separate 1227/96755 bound.

claims.subject: Uniform equilibrium on a rational polyhedral full-core deadlock slice
claims.scope: For any baseline s, including negative coordinates, a completion satisfying IsDeadlockRationalJointBlockCompletion reward s has target deadlockRationalBlockValue s. The predicate fixes the full-core singleton matrix, requires reward({1,3}) = s, and imposes eight explicit collision-cap inequalities; it describes an unbounded nonlocal polyhedral slice, not all full-core completions.

claims.subject: Finite reward-range sufficient condition for stationary quitting equilibria
claims.scope: Strict lower and weak upper conditional reward-range comparisons yield a stationary behavioral terminal Nash and a uniform-equilibrium payoff; the hypotheses are a sufficient source-data condition, not a universal classification.

claims.subject: Cycle-balanced fixed-sign quitting influence tables
claims.scope: Fixed positive, negative, or absent pair influences, with positive sign product on every directed simple influence cycle, produce a literal sure-exit coalition and a uniform-equilibrium payoff against all unilateral behavioral deviations. Within the fixed-sign class, absence of every sure-exit coalition forces a negative simple influence cycle.

claims.subject: Literal strict three-blocker core with arbitrary outside-player payoffs
claims.scope: Passive continuation values and uniform literal strict blocker signs on one three-player core yield an exact stationary all-behavior uniform-equilibrium payoff, with arbitrarily many outside players and unrestricted outside-player reward coordinates. This is the three-core case, not the arbitrary odd-cycle theorem.

claims.subject: Finite quitting games with projective-Q-bar normalized singleton matrix
claims.scope: Ambient projective Q-bar yields a uniform-equilibrium payoff against every unilateral behavioral deviation. The punishment-normal path decoder is constructed through the deleted-survival Snell fork; this does not cover ResidualHardClass.

claims.subject: At-most-one-owner calendars on the Solan--Vieille boundary table
claims.scope: Every arbitrary finite or infinite deterministic calendar with at most one positive quitting hazard per date has literal all-behavior terminal exploitability E satisfying 1 <= 14 E^2 + 67 E and hence E > 1/68. This rules out that strategy architecture on one residual-hard table; the same game has a checked two-owner uniform equilibrium.

claims.subject: Supplied finite-orbit obstruction in quitting-game semantics
claims.scope: The production-semantic individually rational, near-feasible finite-orbit carrier is equivalent to the corresponding arbitrarily-large finite-variation condition. HasQuittingSimonFiniteCellLyapunovCertificate and its direct obstruction adapter consume supplied exact finite-cell data; the combined terminal-gap capstone additionally assumes SuppliedQuittingSimonFiniteOrbitNecessity, exclusion of stationarily generated approximate equilibria, exclusion of instant punishment, and one positive Lyapunov scale. The necessity implication, certificate, and chronological strategy remain unproved.

claims.subject: Sorin's absorbing-game uniform-payoff segment
claims.scope: Every payoff (a, 2(1-a)) with 1/2 <= a <= 2/3 is realized against all unilateral behavioral deviations; the account strategy may depend on the requested accuracy.

quitting_frontier.summary: The quitting proof search has four mechanically checkable open leaves. The general and all-quitting conjectures remain open independently of any one certificate grammar.
